Subject: How to pack a 45L for a weekend trip (and what to leave behind)
CTA: Shop the Cascade 45L -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/products/NB-TRK-01
Body: Hey,

A 45L pack is the sweet spot for a two-night trip. Enough room to carry what you need, not so much that you start justifying extras. The Northbay Cascade 45L (NB-TRK-01) holds exactly that — 45 liters, internal frame, 1.4 kg empty — and it's worth knowing how to fill it well.

**Start with the heavy stuff at your back.**
Sleeping bag at the bottom. Tent body and poles upright along the spine, close to the internal frame. Food bag and bear canister (if required) sit mid-pack, centered and high. This keeps the load close to your center of gravity and off your lower back on longer approaches.

**Layer in the mid-weight items.**
Insulation layer and camp clothes go in next, used to fill gaps around harder items. Cooking kit — stove, pot, fuel — nestled upright if your pot is aluminum, sideways if it's compact. A 45L packs out a 3-season sleep system, a 2P tent, 2 days of food, and a full cook kit without creative compression, as long as none of it is oversized.

**Top-load what you'll reach for first.**
Rain shell on top. Headlamp, first aid kit, and snacks in the lid pocket or hipbelt pockets if you have them. Map or permit in a quick-access spot.

**One note on water resistance.**
The Cascade's ripstop nylon shell handles light rain and trail splash. It is water-resistant, not waterproof — there's a difference. In sustained rain or creek crossings, line the interior with a pack liner or use dry bags for anything you can't afford to get wet. That's not a workaround; that's just how packs work.

**What a 45L is not built for.**
Winter camping with a 0°F bag and extra layers, or any trip where you're bringing more than 3 days of food and full group gear. For those, you'll want more volume. A 45L is a focused tool — it works best when you pack with intention.

45 liters, 1.4 kg, internal frame. Ready when you are.
